newsitem.title: USA: Chase says Q1 revs below target.
newsitem.headline: Chase says Q1 revs below target.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp said Tuesday its first quarter revenue growth fell below target but its financial performance continues strong despite higher credit card charge-offs.
The bank holding company cited improvement in its efficiency ratio and a higher return on equity in the first quarter.
It said expenses declined two percent in the period, reflecting incremental merger savings of $205 million, while return on equity rose to 19.5 percent from 18 percent a year earlier.

Operating net income for global wholesale banking rose five percent in the quarter, it said, reflecting significant revenue growth throughout its global markets businesses, which include trading activities.
Net income from global services rose 21 percent as a result of active new business pipelines in its investor services and global trust businesses.
Nonperforming assets totaled $1.1 billion at the end of the quarter, down slightly from $1.2 billion at the end of 1996 and $1.7 billion a year earlier, it said.

Total consumer net charge-offs grew to $422 million in the first quarter from $315 million a year earlier. Managed credit card net charge-offs were $358 million, or 5.66 percent of average managed receivables, compared with the year-earlier $270 million, or 4.66 percent.

Chase said mortgage banking net income more than doubled in the first quarter. Revenues from Chase Capital partners declined from an "extremely" strong 1996 first quarter but were in line with the last eight quarters, it said.
